(Edited) This is decidedly the best of the few shopping apps to link with Google Assistant. I've splashed out for the Family plan, both for sharing with my family and for customising the store order. PROS: 1. Cross-platform, working (among others) with Android, iOS, and Linux, all important in my household. 2. You can customise both individual grocery items and the display order for each store. This saves a lot of time in each shop. 3. Full integration with Google Assistant, so that anyone in my family can easily ask (e.g. the Nest Mini) to add groceries to the shopping list. Interestingly, the AnyList website's support explains how to integrate with the Google Assistant better than Google's own help does. 4. Impressively rapid synchronisation between devices. CONS: 1. AnyList is expensive compared to other apps of similar complexity, so for the price, I would have expected a better-rounded app. 2. When someone adds, via the Google Assistant (i.e. voice command on the phone or Google Mini), an item that's already on the shopping list, AnyList adds it as another (duplicate) item. There should be a global option to either ignore the item or increase the count, not create a duplicate. 3. Printing is primitive (I don't want to be messing with my phone in the store; paper is much easier, and won't tempt thieves). A medium-length list goes over two pages, and a longer list over three, when it could easily fit on one page over two columns in landscape or portrait. I have to "print" to PDF, then print the PDF on two columns (using my printer's features) to fit on one page. The app also needs some printing options, such as font size and number of columns.
